exercises.title: U5 听力·对话 Lending a Friend Money
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Anna, could you lend me twenty pounds until next week?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Of course. But why do you need it so suddenly?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I want to buy a ticket for the new musical with my sister.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: That sounds lovely. You can pay me back whenever you like.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Thank you. I'll give it back as soon as I get my pocket money.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Don't worry about it. That's what friends are for.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: You're really kind. I'll remember this and help you in return one day.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I know you will. Now go and enjoy the show!

exercises.translation_cn: 汤姆向安娜借20英镑买音乐剧的票,想和姐姐一起去看;安娜爽快答应,说什么时候还都行;汤姆说一拿到零花钱就还,并表示日后定会回报;安娜说朋友就该这样。

exercises.title: U5 听力·短文 A Good Servant, a Bad Master
exercises.speaker: uk_female
exercises.transcript: A famous thinker once said that money is a good servant but a bad master. As a servant, money does useful work for us. It pays for food, books and medicine, and lets us help the people we love. But when people care only about getting more and more, money becomes a master that rules their lives. The real danger is not money itself, but the place we give it in our hearts. A wise person keeps money useful, but never lets it become the most important thing of all.
exercises.translation_cn: 一位著名思想家说过,金钱是好仆人却是坏主人。作为仆人,金钱为我们做有用的事——付食物、书籍、药品的钱,让我们帮助所爱的人;但当人们只在乎不断索取更多时,金钱就成了主宰生活的主人。真正的危险不在金钱本身,而在于我们把它放在心中的位置;明智的人让金钱有用,却绝不让它成为最重要的东西。

options: Makes it the centre of life.

exercises.title: U5 听力·对话 Opening a Savings Account
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Clerk
transcript.text: Good morning. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Girl
transcript.text: I'd like to open a savings account, please. I want to start saving my pocket money.

transcript.speaker: Clerk
transcript.text: That's a wise idea. How much would you like to put in to start?

transcript.speaker: Girl
transcript.text: Just ten pounds for now. I plan to add a little every month.

transcript.speaker: Clerk
transcript.text: Perfect. Saving a small sum regularly is the best habit of all.

transcript.speaker: Girl
transcript.text: My grandfather always says I should save for a rainy day.

transcript.speaker: Clerk
transcript.text: He gives excellent advice. Here is your new account book.

transcript.speaker: Girl
transcript.text: Thank you. I feel quite grown-up now!

exercises.translation_cn: 女孩到银行想开一个储蓄账户,打算把零花钱存起来;职员说这很明智,问她先存多少;女孩说先存10英镑,以后每月再加一点;职员说定期存小钱是最好的习惯;女孩说爷爷常叮嘱她未雨绸缪;职员夸建议很好并递上账户本。

exercises.title: U5 听力·短文 Giving to Charity
exercises.speaker: uk_female
exercises.transcript: Many people choose to give part of their money to charity. They do not expect anything in return; they simply want to help those in need. Even a small gift can make a real difference. Some donate to help sick children, others to build schools or feed the hungry. Giving teaches us that money is not only for ourselves. In fact, people who share often feel happier than those who keep everything. As an old saying goes, kindness is the one gift that grows when you give it away.
exercises.translation_cn: 许多人选择把一部分钱捐给慈善机构。他们不求任何回报,只想帮助有需要的人;哪怕一份小小的捐赠也能带来真正的改变。有人捐助患病的孩子,有人捐建学校或救济饥民。给予让我们懂得,钱不只是为了自己;事实上,乐于分享的人往往比独享一切的人更快乐。正如一句老话所说,善良是唯一一种越给越多的礼物。

exercises.title: U5 听力·对话 Planning the Weekend Spending
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: We've got twenty pounds for the weekend. How should we spend it?

transcript.speaker: Lucy
transcript.text: Let's not waste it all on snacks like last time.

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: Good point. Maybe we should save half and spend the other half.

transcript.speaker: Lucy
transcript.text: I agree. Ten pounds for the cinema, and ten pounds saved.

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: That sounds sensible. What film do you want to watch?

transcript.speaker: Lucy
transcript.text: There's a new one about a poor man who suddenly becomes rich.

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: Perfect. And we can bring our own drinks to save even more.

transcript.speaker: Lucy
transcript.text: Now that's smart thinking. Let's go!

exercises.translation_cn: 本和露西周末有20英镑,讨论怎么花;露西提议别像上次全花在零食上;本建议存一半花一半;两人决定10英镑看电影、10英镑存起来;露西想看一部关于穷人突然变富的新片;本提议自带饮料更省钱;露西夸他想得周到。

exercises.title: U5 听力·短文 A Tip for Spending Wisely
exercises.speaker: uk_female
exercises.transcript: Here is a simple tip for anyone who wants to spend money wisely. Before you buy something, wait one whole day and ask yourself if you really need it. Very often, the strong wish to buy it will quietly go away. This little habit can save you a surprising amount of money over a year. Remember, every coin you do not waste today is a coin you can use for something important tomorrow. Spending wisely is not about being mean; it is about giving your money to the things that truly matter.
exercises.translation_cn: 给想理性花钱的人一个小贴士:买东西前先等一整天,问问自己是否真的需要它;很多时候,那股强烈的购买欲会悄悄消退。这个小习惯一年下来能省下出人意料的一笔钱。记住,你今天没浪费的每一枚硬币,都是明天可用于重要之事的硬币。理性消费不是吝啬,而是把钱花在真正要紧的事情上。
